scope: Primary or authoritative source metadata and exact applicability boundaries for the frozen Wave 32 rooted and rootless-integrally-indecomposable rank-44 endpoint branches.

retention_policy.retained_objects: Bibliographic metadata, stable source URLs, concise paraphrases, chronology, and exact support/non-support boundaries.

records.title: On Clique Graphs and Clique Regular Graphs
records.inspected: Published/preprint metadata, abstract, and the exact Conway-99 clique-graph spectral application through the repository's earlier independent literature audit.
records.supports: For a putative Conway-99 graph, the graph on its 231 triangles with adjacency by intersection has spectrum 18^1, 7^54, 0^44, (-3)^132. This is the strongest exact prior-art hit for the actual triangle-incidence layer.
records.does_not_support: It supplies no integral rank-44 eigenspace lattice, root image of norm 42, ADE primitive closure, indecomposable endpoint classification, Schur-defined Q/B package, graph construction, or nonexistence theorem.

records.title: A Comprehensive Study of Clique Graphs and Clique Regular Graphs
records.inspected: Current title, author, submission date, abstract, Conway-99 motivation, and the regular clique-graph spectral formula.
records.supports: Current expansion of clique-graph theory; its general regular-graph formula specializes to the same conditional 231-triangle spectrum and its introduction still presents the Conway bounty as unclaimed.
records.does_not_support: It does not state the rank-44 integral projector/root-image code, either endpoint branch, the Schur matrix package, or a target resolution.

records.title: On the automorphism group of a putative Conway 99-graph
records.inspected: Publisher abstract, article metadata, and theorem scope through current and prior repository audits.
records.supports: A current refereed primary source explicitly calling existence an elusive open problem and proving conditional automorphism restrictions.
records.does_not_support: Its automorphism hypotheses cannot be imported into the unrestricted endpoint. It neither constructs nor excludes the graph and supplies no root or indecomposable-lattice classification.

records.title: Strongly Regular Graphs
records.venue: Encyclopedia of Mathematics and its Applications 182, Cambridge University Press
records.inspected: Bibliographic record, parameter index/current author-preprint context, and standard association-scheme terminology.
records.supports: Authoritative background for the parameter set, primitive strongly regular graphs, and Bose-Mesner primitive idempotents; its parameter index marks (99,14,1,2) with unknown existence.
records.does_not_support: Graph primitivity and algebraic primitivity of a Bose-Mesner idempotent do not by themselves forbid coordinate blocks or diagonal signs in the full matrix commutant. No frozen endpoint theorem is stated.

records.title: Integral symmetric bilinear forms and some of their applications
records.inspected: Bibliographic metadata and exact proposition scope inherited from the independently checked Wave 28 audit.
records.supports: Standard even-overlattice/isotropic-subgroup correspondence and opposite discriminant forms for primitive orthogonal complements under the stated hypotheses.
records.does_not_support: It does not classify positive-definite rank-44 endpoint forms, root-preserving glue, the 231-coordinate root-image code, or any Schur/incidence realization.

records.title: Reflective Integral Lattices
records.supports: Structural prior art for reflective lattices whose root system has maximal rank, described by a scaled root system and a code in a reduced discriminant group.
records.does_not_support: The frozen rooted endpoint need not be reflective and its roots need not have maximal rank. The article does not classify its partial ADE closure, rootless complement, marked 231-coordinate code, or graph incidence.

records.title: Modular Lattices, Together With A Table of the Best Such Lattices
records.inspected: Definition, similarity equations, strongly modular table scope, and current catalogue context.
records.supports: An N-modular integral lattice is similar to its dual via a norm-multiplier-N similarity. In rank 44 this definition forces determinant N^22 by determinant comparison.
records.does_not_support: The endpoint only has 21L* subset L and determinants 9,21,49,81,189,441,729,1029, so it is not conventionally N-modular for N=3,7,21. The table is not a classification of the weaker containment.

records.title: The Shadow Theory of Modular and Unimodular Lattices
records.inspected: Author-hosted/published abstract, arXiv metadata, and stated strongly modular level set.
records.supports: Sharp minimum/shadow bounds under unimodular or strongly N-modular hypotheses for a specific level set.
records.does_not_support: Level 21 is not in the displayed strongly modular set, and the endpoint has no required similarity. Its bounds or classifications cannot be imported from 21L* subset L.

records.title: Strongly modular lattices with long shadow
records.venue: Journal de Theorie des Nombres de Bordeaux 16(1), 187-196
records.inspected: Publisher metadata, abstract, and definition of strongly N-modular via rescaled partial duals.
records.supports: Classification results for strongly modular lattices with longest and second-longest shadow under explicit partial-dual similarity hypotheses.
records.does_not_support: No such partial-dual similarities are present in the endpoint package. The source does not classify the eight rank-44 determinant rows or either endpoint branch.

records.title: Incremental Algorithms for Lattice Problems
records.inspected: ArXiv and institutional metadata plus abstract.
records.supports: Given a complete generating system containing all lattice vectors through the required bound, the incremental algorithm can determine an orthogonal decomposition and construct indecomposable summands.
records.does_not_support: It is not an enumeration of all even rank-44 forms satisfying the endpoint determinant, scaled-dual, marked-frame, and Schur constraints. Failure to find a decomposition for a candidate does not classify the branch.

records.title: Computing Isometries of Lattices
records.inspected: Bibliographic metadata and abstract-level algorithm scope.
records.supports: Exact algorithmic prior art for testing lattice isometry and automorphisms of supplied positive-definite forms.
records.does_not_support: It does not enumerate the unrestricted rank-44 endpoint, produce an automorphism, or justify assuming any symmetry or catalogue representative.

records.title: Additively Indecomposable Positive Definite Integral Lattices
records.inspected: Publisher metadata, abstract, keywords, and stated discriminant range.
records.supports: Recent criteria connecting ordinary indecomposability to the distinct stronger notion of additive indecomposability for discriminants 2, 3, 4, and 5.
records.does_not_support: The frozen branch asks only for absence of an integral orthogonal direct sum and has determinant at least 9. The article neither classifies that branch nor supplies the frame/Schur/incidence package.

records.title: Frames over Finite Fields: Equiangular Lines in Orthogonal Geometry
records.inspected: Abstract and Example 5.5 context inherited from prior independent audits.
records.supports: Related graph/frame prior art: a hypothetical Conway graph yields an equiangular tight frame of 100 vectors in a 45-dimensional space over F5.
records.does_not_support: That finite-field 100-by-45 object is categorically different from the real integral 231-by-44 endpoint and has no frozen root-image, Q/B, or incidence certificate.

records.title: Clique complexes of strongly regular graphs, their eigenvalues, and cohomology groups
records.inspected: Publisher/arXiv metadata and abstract; the June 2026 follow-up arXiv:2606.27328 was also inspected at abstract level.
records.supports: Current general spectral and topological work on triangle/clique complexes of strongly regular graphs.
records.does_not_support: No inspected target-specific rank-44 root lattice, integral projector, primitive idempotent commutant, or endpoint classification was found. General clique homology is not the frozen 231-triangle Schur package.

records.title: Approaching the Conway-99 problem using SAT solvers
records.inspected: Current arXiv metadata and scope already recorded in SOURCES.bib and the independently verified Wave 28 literature audit; the independent Wave 32 source verifier flagged its omission from the first frozen metadata set.
records.supports: Current computational prior art reporting that the tested SAT approaches were infeasible at the stated resource scale.
records.does_not_support: It proves neither existence nor nonexistence, supplies no checked negative certificate, and does not resolve either frozen endpoint branch.

conclusion.strongest_exact_prior_art_hit: Petro-Phillips conditionally derives the actual target triangle-intersection spectrum; this was already public and recorded in the repository before Wave 32.
